box + point prompts → pixel masks (two passes)

adp.meaning_of_absence: No qualifying satellite detection. Does NOT mean there is no haze or smoke.

spark.scene: True-color view of the main Hawaiian Islands from Kauai in the northwest to Hawaii Island in the southeast. Scattered to broken white trade-wind cumulus and cirrus cover much of the ocean, especially west and south, with clearer dark ocean in the channels. Hawaii Island is mostly visible with brown interior and white orographic clouds along its eastern and southern flanks. No distinct gray or brown haze, smoke or volcanic plume distinguishable from ordinary white cloud and ocean.

classify.caveats: No plume found; nothing to classify.

volcano_status.source: USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory notices via HANS public API (https://volcanoes.usgs.gov/hans-public/api/search/search)

kilauea.activity_summary: The Halema'uma'u eruption at the summit of Kīlauea is paused following lava fountaining episode 57. Forecast models indicate the next episode is likely sometime between December 4 and 14. Overview: Last night, glow was observed at both the north and southwest eruptive vents in Halema'uma'u, where strong degassing has persisted since the end of Kīlauea summit lava fountaining episode 57 on November 23.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts were within typical levels in October, and minor inflation continues. Mauna Loa had a slight increase in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 66 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the October reporting period, after 53 in September. These variations are within the typical range for the past two years.
